seo.title: Amazon DynamoDB GUI for {devices}
seo.description: Browse DynamoDB tables through a planner that picks Query or Scan from your filters, edit items with their types intact, and run PartiQL or API requests.

header.title: Amazon DynamoDB GUI
header.lead: Browse items, read by key with the consumed capacity in view, and edit typed values or run PartiQL.

bands.title: Connect
text: Choose an Auth Method and AWS Region: an access key with an optional session token, an AWS CLI profile or AWS IAM Identity Center. Profiles resolve credential_process helpers and role_arn chains, and every request goes over HTTPS, signed with Signature Version 4, so there is no SSL setting and no SSH tunnel.

For DynamoDB Local, run docker run -p 8000:8000 amazon/dynamodb-local and choose DynamoDB Local (no credentials); a custom endpoint may use plain HTTP only on this Mac. A region in another AWS partition, such as China, reaches its own endpoint without a custom one. The setup guide lists the IAM actions each task needs.

bands.title: Read, filter and edit items
text: Key filters run as a Query and other filters as a Scan, which reads and bills the whole table; the status bar shows the operation, the returned and scanned item counts and the consumed read capacity. Sort-key filters become key conditions where they can, and nested paths such as address.city work. Clicking the sort key’s header on a Query of one partition makes DynamoDB return items in that order.

Columns come from the items: the keys, attributes found in a sample of the first items, and those on the page in view. Maps, lists and sets open in the JSON editor, numbers keep every digit, Set NULL removes an attribute, and each row saves as one PartiQL statement that refuses to overwrite a concurrent change. The editor takes PartiQL, or an action name such as Query or TransactWriteItems followed by its request JSON; throttled requests retry with backoff.

bands.title: Tables, indexes and settings
text: New Table… sets the keys, capacity mode, table class, deletion protection and secondary indexes, and previews the CreateTable request; a local secondary index can only be defined there. The Structure tab adds or drops one global secondary index per save, and the DDL tab shows the request that recreates the table.
<ui>Maintenance</ui> covers point-in-time recovery, deletion protection, the stream, the table class, switching to on-demand capacity and turning Time to Live off.

moveData: Write items from the editor with a PartiQL INSERT or a BatchWriteItem request, which resends unprocessed items. Export a table or a result as {exportFormats}.

faq.question: How do I keep a read from scanning the whole table?
faq.answer: Filter on the partition key with =, or on a global index’s partition key with a filter on each of its sort keys, and the read runs as a Query. A keys-only index is not used for browsing, so query it from the editor with a Query request that names its IndexName.

faq.question: How do I change an item’s key?
faq.answer: Use <ui>Duplicate Row</ui>, which copies every attribute but the keys, give the copy its new key, save, then delete the original.

faq.question: Are grid edits saved in one transaction?
faq.answer: No. Each changed row is written on its own. Put writes that must succeed together in an ExecuteTransaction or TransactWriteItems request in the editor.
